questions.prompt: What are the five primary categories of sensory receptors based on the type of stimulus that activates them?
questions.modelAnswer: Mechanoreceptors, photoreceptors, chemoreceptors, thermoreceptors, and nociceptors.

questions.prompt: Define the process of "sensory transduction."
questions.modelAnswer: The process of converting an environmental stimulus (e.g., pressure, light) into electrical energy (a receptor potential).

questions.prompt: How does a receptor potential differ from a standard action potential in terms of its electrical nature and potential for summation?
questions.modelAnswer: A receptor potential is a graded, local potential change that can be summated, whereas an action potential is an "all-or-none" propagating event.

questions.prompt: Which principle explains why a dedicated sensory pathway always produces the same perceived sensation regardless of where the stimulus is applied along the nerve?
questions.modelAnswer: The "labeled line" principle (or Law of Specific Nerve Energies).

questions.prompt: Define a "receptive field" as it pertains to a sensory neuron.
questions.modelAnswer: An area of the body that, when stimulated, changes the firing rate of a sensory neuron.

questions.prompt: What is the primary physiological function of lateral inhibition in sensory relay nuclei?
questions.modelAnswer: To sharpen the boundaries and localization of a stimulus by providing contrast through the inhibition of surrounding neurons.

questions.prompt: Contrast "phasic" and "tonic" receptors regarding the specific information they encode about a stimulus.
questions.modelAnswer: Phasic receptors adapt rapidly and encode stimulus velocity (changes); tonic receptors adapt slowly and encode stimulus intensity and duration.

questions.prompt: Which mechanoreceptor is characterized as being very rapidly adapting and specialized for the detection of high-frequency vibration?
questions.modelAnswer: Pacinian corpuscle.

questions.prompt: Which encapsulated mechanoreceptor has small receptive fields and is essential for two-point discrimination on glabrous skin?
questions.modelAnswer: Meissner corpuscle.

questions.prompt: Describe the difference between Ruffini corpuscles and Merkel receptors in terms of their receptive field size and stimulus modality.
questions.modelAnswer: Ruffini corpuscles have large receptive fields and detect stretch; Merkel receptors have small receptive fields and detect vertical indentation/steady pressure.

questions.prompt: List the lettered nerve fiber classifications (A, B, and C) in order of their relative conduction velocity from fastest to slowest.
questions.modelAnswer: A (fastest), B (medium), C (slowest).

questions.prompt: In the Lloyd and Hunt numerical classification for sensory fibers, which group corresponds to unmyelinated fibers carrying slow pain and temperature?
questions.modelAnswer: Group IV (C fibers).

questions.prompt: Which specific somatosensory modalities are carried exclusively by the Dorsal Column-Medial Lemniscal system?
questions.modelAnswer: Fine touch, pressure, vibration, two-point discrimination, and proprioception.

questions.prompt: Which specific somatosensory modalities are carried primarily by the Anterolateral (spinothalamic) system?
questions.modelAnswer: Pain, temperature, and light (crude) touch.

questions.prompt: At which specific anatomical location do the second-order neurons of the Dorsal Column system cross the midline?
questions.modelAnswer: In the medulla oblongata (as internal arcuate fibers from the nuclei gracilis and cuneatus).

questions.prompt: At which specific anatomical location do the second-order neurons of the Anterolateral system cross the midline?
questions.modelAnswer: In the spinal cord (within a few segments of entry, via the ventral white commissure).

questions.prompt: Name the specific thalamic relay nucleus for somatosensory information originating from the body.
questions.modelAnswer: Ventral posterolateral (VPL) nucleus.

questions.prompt: What determines the relative size of the representation of a body part on the somatosensory homunculus in the cortex?
questions.modelAnswer: The density of sensory receptors (sensory unit innervation) in that specific body part.

questions.prompt: Which specific transient receptor potential (TRP) channel is activated by both warm temperatures and capsaicin?
questions.modelAnswer: TRPV1 (vanilloid receptor).

questions.prompt: Where are the cell bodies of first-order somatosensory neurons typically found?
questions.modelAnswer: In the dorsal root ganglia or cranial nerve ganglia.
